title: Cross-SDK credential presets, stream iterator sanity fixes, and synchronized SDK version bump
author: Samir Nair
description: Motivation: teams reported inconsistent behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs when using credential rotation presets and when resuming/consuming streaming iterators. This PR centralizes the credential preset schema, introduces conservative default backoff profiles, and stabilizes streaming iterator edge cases (nil/None reads, canceled contexts, and EOF+error races). The changes are intended to be strictly additive and ergonomic: they surface a small set of named credential profiles (static, rotating-short, rotating-long, delegated) that map to documented backoff/retry semantics; they harmonize stream iterator APIs across SDKs so examples and client code can be shared; and they bump SDK package versions in lockstep to avoid downstream parity issues. Checklist: - [x] Add credential preset schema and mapping in go/py/ts SDKs - [x] Implement conservative retry/backoff presets and document expected SLOs - [x] Fix Go iterator nil-pointer race and add unit test - [x] Align Python iterator to raise StopAsyncIteration consistently on clean EOF - [x] Ensure TypeScript pull-generator yields identical envelope shapes for errors vs data - [x] Update examples and migration guide - [x] Run cross-language integration tests and iterate on flaky TS test - [x] Bump versions: python 1.8.0, typescript 1.8.0, go v1.8.0 Summary of what changed: - Introduced a small credentials module/surface in each SDK exposing preset profiles and a lightweight adapter for custom credential providers. The adapter includes a recommended prefetch window and a graceful fallback order (delegated -> rotating-short -> static). - Consolidated retry templates: added "conservative" and "aggressive" presets. Conservative is default for streaming; aggressive for batch/embeddings. - Streaming iterator fixes: Go: race on iterator.Close when consumer canceled was causing intermittent panics; added a mutex and nil-check, and more robust context cancellation handling. Python: normalized StopAsyncIteration behavior and added a small compatibility shim for older consumers. TypeScript: unified error envelopes so consumers do not need separate parsing logic for partial-chunk errors. - Tests: added unit tests for each SDK and an integration fixture that exercises credential rotation during a stream restart. - Docs & examples: updated migration guide (docs/sdk-migration.md) and per-SDK README examples to show new preset usage. Commits (high level): - feat(auth): add credential preset matrix and adapter (py/ts/go) - feat(retry): add conservative/aggressive retry templates and docs - fix(go/stream): iterator nil-check & cancellation race guard - fix(ts/stream): unify error envelope + resume semantics - fix(py/stream): normalize StopAsyncIteration and add shim - test: add crosslang integration test exercising rotation during stream resume - chore: bump sdk versions to 1.8.0 (py/ts/go) Files touched (representative): [sdks/python/redwood_sdk/credentials.py, sdks/python/redwood_sdk/stream/iterator.py, sdks/python/setup.py, sdks/typescript/src/credentials/presets.ts, sdks/typescript/src/stream/asyncGenerator.ts, sdks/typescript/package.json, sdks/go/credentials/presets.go, sdks/go/stream/iterator.go, docs/sdk-migration.md, tests/integration/stream_retry_rotation_test.py] CI notes: CI ran matrix builds for py/ts/go. Unit test matrices passed. Integration-TS initially had one flaky test (stream-restart-race) that failed on the first run, flakiness reproduced locally; added 200ms jitter in the harness and re-ran — subsequent run passed. All linters green. Impact/Rollout: This is a backward-compatible improvement with clearer ergonomics for auth+streaming. We recommend publishing coordinated SDK releases (1.8.0) together and notifying users of the new preset names and minor behavioral normalization for streaming EOF semantics. Quick migration tips are included in docs/sdk-migration.md.

Samir Nair (author): Conservative preset is opt-in for Hosted by default; SDKs default to conservative for streaming but we documented the behavior and added migration guide. We included a feature flag in the host-side config for gradual rollout.
Owen Brooks: Go change looks good; can you add a short comment above the guard explaining the historical race? Also please add a small benchmark showing no CPU regression.
Samir Nair: Added comment and a microbenchmark; no measurable regression in our perf harness.
Priya Raman: TS integration used to rely on yielding partial error chunks; with a unified envelope we might break some consumers. Add a small adapter in examples to ease migration.
Samir Nair: Added adapter example in examples/ts/adapter-migration.md and updated README.
Maya Chen: Approving pending green CI and the small docs tweak.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash after CI pass and approvals. Release coordinator will cut SDK packages together.
release_notes: Add credential preset profiles (static, rotating-short, rotating-long, delegated); conservative and aggressive retry templates; normalize streaming iterator EOF/StopAsyncIteration across SDKs; fix Go iterator cancellation race; unified TypeScript error envelopes for streams; coordinated SDK version bump to 1.8.0 for Python/TypeScript/Go; migration guide and adapter examples included.
notes_for_changelog: SDKs: auth: credential presets + retry templates; streaming: EOF semantics normalized and Go nil-check fix; examples/migration guide updated; versions bumped to 1.8.0.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: some clients may rely on previous TS partial-error envelopes. Mitigation: adapter example + migration guide, opt-in feature gate on host for preset defaults, staged rollout and monitoring on Console.
testing_summary: Added unit tests in each SDK and a cross-language integration fixture. Ran full CI matrix and re-ran flaky TS integration after harness jitter fix. Microbenchmark added for Go iterator guard showed <1% CPU regression under sustained load.
